path.description: CUTLASS 3.x stream-K (sm90 and, through the same params, sm100): stream-K units that do not own the final split write their partial accumulator to a per-tile workspace and later units add onto it (BlockStripedReduce::reduce, an ordinary load-add-store). ReductionMode::Deterministic makes unit K_idx wait until exactly K_idx peers have arrived (wait_eq), so the additions happen in K order; ReductionMode::Nondeterministic waits only for the first peer (wait_lt) so partials accumulate in arrival order.

gate.note: Deterministic is A2 (turnstile in K order). Nondeterministic is class A. Callers can flip it: SGLang's FP8 blockwise sm90 GEMM sets Nondeterministic (see the sglang inventory).

evidence.claim: if reduction_mode_ == Deterministic: wait_eq(lock, K_idx) else wait_lt(lock, 1); then BlockStripedReduceT::reduce(workspace, accumulators)
arrive_inc after the reduce increments the lock by k_tile_count (or 1 with separate reduction)
the unit that owns the final split waits for K_idx peers and load_adds the workspace (fixed order)

notes: No atomicAdd on floats: the RMW is plain and the barrier decides the order. The only atomics are the integer barrier operations (cutlass-0004).

path.description: Stream-K with separate reduction units: a reduction unit waits until all num_peers partials are in the workspace, then sums them in peer index order (separate_reduction, lines 569-573).

CUTLASS 2.x stream-K (GemmUniversalStreamk, ThreadblockSwizzleStreamK): the first peer stores its partial tile to the workspace and later peers add onto it. With ReductionStrategy kAtomic the peers wait only for initialisation (wait_lt, arrival order); with kMixed they wait for the previous peer (turnstile, fixed order) or use separate reduction.

gate.note: kAtomic is documented at line 78 as 'Non-deterministic reduction of SK-block partials using atomic aggregation in L2' and is not the default. vLLM's scaled_mm_c2x uses this swizzle with the default strategy.

evidence.claim: kAtomic: wait_lt(first_block_idx, 1); otherwise wait_eq(first_block_idx, block_idx - first_block_idx); then BlockStripedReduceT::reduce
enum ReductionStrategy { kNone, kAtomic, kMixed }; static ReductionStrategy const kReductionStrategy = kMixed
separate_reduction waits wait_eq_reset(num_peers) then reduces the workspace

notes: Default path is deterministic (A2). Class A only if a caller instantiates the swizzle with kAtomic, which is a compile-time constant at this sha.

path.description: Barrier primitive used by stream-K fixup, split-K and FlashAttention-3's deterministic mode: red.relaxed.gpu.global.add.s32 (or atomicAdd) on the lock word; wait_eq/wait_lt spin with ld.acquire; wait_eq_reset uses atomicCAS (line 175).

notes: Exact integer counter; it is what imposes the fixed order in the A2 rows above.

path.description: Parallel split-K reduction kernel (GemmUniversalMode::kGemmSplitKParallel): each partition's partial tile is written to a workspace by the GEMM, and this kernel sums the partitions in index order k = 0..partitions-1 into the output.

evidence.claim: for (k = 0; k < partitions; k += kPartitionsPerStage) load workspace fragments then accumulator = reduction_op(accumulator, workspace_frag[i]) in order

notes: Fixed order; no atomics. This is the 'splitKreduce' design the taxonomy calls A3-by-design; recorded as A2 because the order is serial by construction rather than gated.

path.description: EVT column/row reduction fusion (sm90): each output tile writes its partial column (or row, line 1992) reduction to a workspace, increments an integer tile counter, and the tile that observes the last count performs the final reduction over the workspace.

downstream.argument: Which tile performs the final reduction depends on arrival, but the final reduction loops over the workspace slots in index order (end() after line 1517), and every partial is written to its own slot, so the summation order does not depend on which tile arrived last. The IsAtomic variant of the same visitor (not present in the scanned candidates as float atomics) would be class A; at this sha the only atomic here is the integer counter.

evidence.claim: row-reduction twin of the same counter

notes: The IsAtomic template branch (atomic accumulation into the output) was not exercised by any engine kernel found in this census; confidence medium because the final-reduction loop body after line 1530 was not read line by line.
